items.title: Jane Monheit interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 20, 2010
items.q: I was lucky enough to get an interview with Nancy Wilson

ctx.x: My voice teacher and it’s true. I speak with relatively bad vocal technique. I speak in too low of a voice. I let my voice break. I should be speaking up here clearly like this, but never remember to do it. I never do. I’ve got to work on that.

When I spoke with — I was lucky enough to get an interview with Nancy Wilson and she said that she just wanted to be known as “a singer.” She felt I guess that she’d been typecast as a jazz singer, but that’s not how she felt about herself. You on the other hand have said, “I’m a jazz singer.” So what makes that? Is it the repertoire you choose?

Well you know what, the definition of what makes a jazz singer now has loosened and expanded so completely. And you know what, I’m a lot of different kinds of singers. I mean there’s so much that I love to do. I mean I could call myself a jazz singer. I could call myself a musical theater singer because I can do that too. I could call myself a pop singer because I can do that too. It’s just that jazz is really the center. It’s what I really grew up doing and it’s what suits me the best and it’s what I do for a…
